output.summary: A conifer native to high-elevation habitats from southwestern through central and southeastern Europe, it has dark green needles in pairs and nut-brown cones. Its young cones and buds are gathered wild in spring and made into syrup by drying them through summer into autumn, then boiling the dripped liquid with sugar; they may instead be macerated in sugar and fermented.
output.edibilityNote: Young cones and buds are wild-harvested in spring, then dried and boiled with sugar for syrup, or macerated in sugar, fermented and strained.
